page: Amazon Web Services m9g.16xlarge is a general-purpose, 64-vCPU instance powered by the ARMv9 AWS Graviton architecture with Neoverse-V3 cores. Built on the AWS Nitro System hypervisor, the server provides 64 dedicated physical cores operating at 3.3 GHz without hardware multithreading (one thread per core). Memory capacity totals 256.0 GB of RAM, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory allocation of 4.0 GB per core. The instance includes 34 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth. It does not bundle local NVMe or SSD storage, requiring network-attached storage solutions, and contains no hardware accelerators or GPUs.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong compute scalability and memory performance. The 64 dedicated physical cores achieve top-tier ratings in Geekbench multi-core (30,217.0), single-core (2,383.0), and software compilation via Clang (104,139.0). Stress-ng multi-core testing reached 127,950.05, placing it in the top 25%. Memory throughput is exceptional, marked by 9,281.17 GB/sec on cached read blocks and top-tier PassMark memory scores (4,594.11). Data processing indicators are similarly elevated, showing top-tier performance in PassMark database operations (58,750.24), Redis SET throughput (183.27 million operations/sec), and static web serving throughput (179.08 GB/sec). Single-threaded and multi-threaded compression metrics via gzip and bzip3 also placed within the top 10%.

The absence of hyperthreading eliminates resource contention between virtual threads, resulting in consistent compute efficiency. However, the architecture exhibits distinct tradeoffs. As an arm64-only system without AVX or AMX instruction extensions, it relies on ARM NEON and cryptographic extensions. Without a discrete GPU, generative LLM text generation throughput is restricted, achieving only 9.76 tokens/sec on 135M parameter models and 10.9 tokens/sec on 7B models. Furthermore, without local storage, high-throughput I/O requires network storage optimization.

Given its high core count, extensive memory bandwidth, and 256.0 GB RAM profile, the m9g.16xlarge is well-positioned for large-scale enterprise microservices, in-memory caching layers such as Redis, large CI/CD software compilation pipelines, high-concurrency web serving, and relational or distributed database deployments.
